```{python}
# Quarto's docx template prints author names only, so the affiliations, addresses
# and corresponding-author email that IJPDS requires are rebuilt here from this
# document's own front matter (the YAML above stays the single source of truth).
# The block is shown only in the docx; the HTML title block already carries it.
import yaml
_meta = yaml.safe_load(open("paper.qmd").read().split("---")[1])
_lines = ["**Author affiliations**", ""]
for _a in _meta["author"]:
    _head = f"**{_a['name']}**"
    if _a.get("corresponding"):
        _head += " (corresponding author)"
    if _a.get("orcid"):
        _head += f", ORCID {_a['orcid']}"
    _lines.append("| " + _head)  # pandoc line block: one line per address part
    for _aff in _a.get("affiliations", []):
        _place = " ".join(p for p in (_aff.get("city"), _aff.get("region"), _aff.get("postal-code")) if p)
        _parts = (_aff.get("department"), _aff.get("name"), _aff.get("address"), _place or None, _aff.get("country"))
        _lines.append("| " + ", ".join(p for p in _parts if p))
    if _a.get("email"):
        _lines.append(f"| Email: {_a['email']}")
    _lines.append("")
print("\n".join(_lines))
```

```{python}
#| label: load-summaries
# Small committed summaries written by pipeline/build_cohorts.py, plus the design
# targets from config.yaml. Every number in the prose below is one of these
# variables; nothing is typed by hand.
import json
import pandas as pd
import yaml
pop      = json.load(open("results/population_summary.json"))
manifest = json.load(open("results/release_manifest.json"))
cfg      = yaml.safe_load(open("config.yaml"))

def n(x):
    return f"{int(x):,}"

fl_pool             = n(pop["fl_pool_last_seen"])       # every simulant ever recorded in Florida, once
fl_finder_pool      = n(pop["fl_residents_finder_year"])
finder_year         = pop["finder_year"]
fl_simulants        = n(pop["fl_simulants"])            # 2020 census residents, for the official-count check
registry_rows       = n(manifest["files"]["registry.csv"]["rows"])
finder_500k_rows    = n(manifest["files"]["finder_500k.csv"]["rows"])
finder_100k_rows    = n(manifest["files"]["finder_100k.csv"]["rows"])
overlap_500k_target = n(cfg["cohorts"]["overlap_500k_target"])
overlap_100k_target = n(cfg["cohorts"]["overlap_100k_target"])

# The Key Features quote the design targets as facts about the files, which is
# only honest while the build hits them exactly; fail the render otherwise.
for k in ("500k", "100k"):
    assert manifest["overlaps"][f"finder_{k}"]["overlap_simulants"] == cfg["cohorts"][f"overlap_{k}_target"]
assert manifest["overlaps"]["finder_finder_simulants"] == cfg["cohorts"]["overlap_finder_finder_target"]

# --- everything else the prose quotes, named as in OUTLINE.md's computed-values table ---
err   = json.load(open("results/error_rates.json"))["realised"]
lb    = json.load(open("results/linkage_baseline.json"))
pairs = json.load(open("results/pair_agreement.json"))["finder_500k.csv"]
qa    = json.load(open("results/age_sex_qa.json"))["registry.csv"]
env   = json.load(open("results/environment.json"))
fcds  = pd.read_csv(cfg["paths"]["age_sex_target"], comment="#")

def pct(x, d=1):
    return f"{100 * x:.{d}f}%"

files, ov = manifest["files"], manifest["overlaps"]
registry_simulants     = n(files["registry.csv"]["distinct_simulants"])
registry_dupe_rows     = manifest["registry_duplicate_rows"]
finder_500k_simulants  = n(files["finder_500k.csv"]["distinct_simulants"])
finder_100k_simulants  = n(files["finder_100k.csv"]["distinct_simulants"])
overlap_500k_simulants = n(ov["finder_500k"]["overlap_simulants"])
overlap_100k_simulants = n(ov["finder_100k"]["overlap_simulants"])
overlap_500k_pairs     = n(ov["finder_500k"]["true_pairs"])
overlap_100k_pairs     = n(ov["finder_100k"]["true_pairs"])
overlap_finder_finder  = ov["finder_finder_simulants"]
match_prevalence_500k  = round(ov["finder_500k"]["match_prevalence"], 3)
fl_share_census        = pct(pop["fl_share_census"])
pop_ssn_never          = pct(pop["pop_ssn_never"], 2)
registry_ssn_missing   = pct(err["registry.csv"]["ssn_missing"], 2)
finder_ssn_missing     = pct(err["finder_500k.csv"]["ssn_missing"])
err_ssn_transposed     = n(err["finder_500k.csv"]["ssn_transposed"])
size_registry_mb, size_finder500k_mb, size_finder100k_mb, size_zip_mb = (
    f"{files['registry.csv']['size_bytes'] / 1e6:.0f}", f"{files['finder_500k.csv']['size_bytes'] / 1e6:.0f}",
    f"{files['finder_100k.csv']['size_bytes'] / 1e6:.0f}", f"{manifest['zip']['size_bytes'] / 1e6:.0f}")
md5_registry, md5_finder500k, md5_finder100k, md5_zip = (
    files["registry.csv"]["md5"], files["finder_500k.csv"]["md5"], files["finder_100k.csv"]["md5"], manifest["zip"]["md5"])

co, se, no = cfg["cohorts"], cfg["seeds"], cfg["noise"]
cfg_registry_target, cfg_finder_500k_target, cfg_finder_100k_target = n(co["registry_target"]), n(co["finder_500k_target"]), n(co["finder_100k_target"])
cfg_oversample = co["oversample"]
cfg_seed_sample, cfg_seed_registry, cfg_seed_finder, cfg_seed_postprocess = se["duckdb_sample"], se["psp_registry"], se["psp_finder"], se["postprocess"]
cfg_finder_ssn_missing, cfg_finder_ssn_transposed, cfg_finder_address_missing = pct(no["finder"]["ssn_missing"], 0), pct(no["finder"]["ssn_transposed"], 0), pct(no["finder"]["address_missing"], 0)
cfg_registry_ssn_missing, cfg_registry_ssn_transposed, cfg_registry_address_missing = pct(no["registry"]["ssn_missing"], 0), pct(no["registry"]["ssn_transposed"], 0), pct(no["registry"]["address_missing"], 0)

# deterministic ladder on the 500k finder file (results/linkage_baseline.json)
lb500  = lb["finder_files"]["finder_500k.csv"]
rules  = {r["rule"]: r for r in lb500["rules"]}
def rule(name, key):
    return round(rules[name][key], 4)
r500_name_dob_precision, r500_name_dob_recall = rule("name_dob", "precision"), rule("name_dob", "recall")
r500_name_dob_missed        = round(1 - rules["name_dob"]["recall"], 4)
r500_ssn_only_precision     = rule("ssn_only", "precision")
r500_ssn_only_missed        = round(1 - rules["ssn_only"]["recall"], 4)
r500_fcds_min_ssn_recall    = rule("fcds_min_ssn", "recall")
r500_fcds_min_monthyear_precision = rule("fcds_min_monthyear", "precision")
r500_fcds_min_monthyear_fp  = n(rules["fcds_min_monthyear"]["predicted_pairs"] - round(rules["fcds_min_monthyear"]["recall"] * lb500["true_pairs"]))
r500_fcds_either_recall, r500_fcds_either_precision = rule("fcds_min_either", "recall"), rule("fcds_min_either", "precision")
r500_fcds_current_recall    = rule("fcds_current_dob_ssn", "recall")
r500_best_recall, r500_best_precision = rule("name_dob_or_ssn", "recall"), rule("name_dob_or_ssn", "precision")
r500_best_missed            = round(1 - rules["name_dob_or_ssn"]["recall"], 4)
r500_lastname_dob_precision = rule("lastname_dob", "precision")
baseline_seconds_500k       = lb500["seconds"]

# agreement among true pairs (results/pair_agreement.json)
pa = pairs["fields"]
agree_first_name_500k, blank_first_name_500k = pct(pa["first_name"]["agree_when_both_present"]), pct(pa["first_name"]["blank_on_either_side"])
agree_last_name_500k,  blank_last_name_500k  = pct(pa["last_name"]["agree_when_both_present"]), pct(pa["last_name"]["blank_on_either_side"])
agree_dob_500k,        blank_dob_500k        = pct(pa["date_of_birth"]["agree_when_both_present"]), pct(pa["date_of_birth"]["blank_on_either_side"])
agree_street_name_500k, blank_street_name_500k = pct(pa["street_name"]["agree_when_both_present"]), pct(pa["street_name"]["blank_on_either_side"])
agree_ssn_500k,        blank_ssn_500k        = pct(pa["ssn"]["agree_when_both_present"]), pct(pa["ssn"]["blank_on_either_side"])
name_dob_all_agree_500k = pct(pairs["name_dob_all_agree"])
ssn_usable_500k         = pct(pairs["ssn_usable_and_agree"])

# age/sex QA, FCDS table facts, environment
age_sex_max_dev     = round(qa["max_abs_share_deviation_pct"], 3)
by_year             = qa["rows_by_census_year"]
registry_share_2040 = pct(by_year["2040"] / sum(by_year.values()), 0)
fcds_rate_min, fcds_rate_max = round(fcds["rate"].min(), 2), round(fcds["rate"].max(), 2)
duckdb_version, psp_version, dataset_version = env["duckdb"], env["pseudopeople"], manifest["version"]
build_wall_seconds, build_peak_gb = round(env["build_wall_seconds"]), round(env["peak_rss_mb"] / 1024, 1)
```

## Key Features {.unnumbered}

- **What is unique:** a large, fully simulated, multi-file dataset for linking individual people, with cross-file ground truth (every record carries a `simulant_id`, so missed-match and false-match rates of any method can be computed exactly rather than estimated), designed to capture the record matching challenges faced by a Florida-scale cancer data system.

- **Why created:** linkage software for cancer registries must be developed and tested on names, dates of birth, addresses and SSNs, which are exactly the identifiers that confidentiality rules prevent registries from releasing.

- **Details:** a simulated Florida drawn from the `{python} fl_pool` simulants recorded as residents in the simulated 2020, 2030 or 2040 censuses, including a registry stand-in of `{python} registry_rows` records whose age and sex distribution is that of the cases reported by the Florida Cancer Data System, and researcher finder files of `{python} finder_500k_rows` and `{python} finder_100k_rows` records drawn from residents in `{python} finder_year`.

- **Data linkage:** the larger finder file includes `{python} overlap_500k_target` simulants in the registry and the smaller finder file includes `{python} overlap_100k_target` simulants. There is no overlap between the finder files.

- **Main categories of data:** simulated person-level identifiers including name, date of birth, sex, street-address fields, SSN, race/ethnicity, and a diagnosis date on each registry record, carrying realistic synthetic noise (typos, nicknames, month/day swaps, blanks, duplications).

- **Access:** direct download under a permissive licence with a DOI.

# Results {#sec-results}

## Structure, contents, and where the data are held {#sec-structure}

The resource is three comma-separated files, deposited on Zenodo under a DOI that will be minted at acceptance <!-- OUTLINE run-list item 10 --> and described in @tbl-release: a registry stand-in of `{python} registry_simulants` simulated people and two finder files of `{python} finder_500k_simulants` and `{python} finder_100k_simulants`. All three are drawn from the `{python} fl_pool` simulants ever recorded as Florida residents in the simulated 2020, 2030 or 2040 census (@sec-methods), a pool that includes people who had died or left the state by the time of the later censuses, as a registry's caseload does. As one external check of scale, the 2020 census slice alone holds `{python} fl_simulants` simulants, which is `{python} fl_share_census` of the official 2020 count of `{python} n(pop["fl_census_2020"])` Floridians <!-- TODO: Census Bureau citation, OUTLINE needs-verification #3 -->. The geography is Florida only, at the granularity of city and ZIP code, and the street addresses are simulated and cannot be geocoded; registry records carry a diagnosis date in 2020, 2030 or 2040, the finder files describe residents of `{python} finder_year`, and there are no county, tract or facility identifiers and no tumour variables, a scope we return to in @sec-discussion.

Rows and people are not quite the same count, and the difference is deliberate. The registry holds `{python} registry_rows` rows for `{python} registry_simulants` distinct simulants, because pseudopeople's duplication noise, which copies a child's record onto a guardian's response, occasionally emits two rows for one person; it touches an old registry only `{python} registry_dupe_rows` times among `{python} registry_simulants` people, so the files are unique to within those rows, which is close to the uniqueness FCDS expects of its own data [@pseudopeople_issue205]. We define overlap once, as the number of distinct simulants present in both a finder file and the registry, and report true record pairs separately where they serve as the denominator of recall (@sec-difficulty); in this release the two counts coincide. The larger finder file shares `{python} overlap_500k_simulants` people with the registry and the smaller `{python} overlap_100k_simulants`, both exactly as designed, and the two finder files share `{python} overlap_finder_finder` people with each other, so the smaller file is a clean held-out replicate of the larger.

This exactness was not free. An earlier build trimmed the oversampled cohorts without stratifying by overlap status, overshot both overlap targets by roughly a third and left the two finder files sharing people they were designed not to share, an error that scoring against the identity key caught before anything was released; the released build trims within strata (@sec-methods) and hits every design count. We publish MD5 and SHA-256 digests for each file and for the bundle, so that a user can prove the file in hand is the file profiled here, and we record every seed so that the build can be repeated; at the time of writing the current design has been built once, so the checksums are there to let reproducibility be checked rather than to claim it has been demonstrated.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-release
#| tbl-cap: "The released files: people and rows, designed overlaps, blank shares against their targets, size and MD5 digest. SHA-256 digests are in the manifest deposited with the files."
#| output: asis
def blank(file, field, target):
    return f"{pct(target, 0)} → {pct(err[file][field], 2 if file == 'registry.csv' else 1)}"
rows = [
    ("registry.csv", registry_rows, registry_simulants, "—",
     blank("registry.csv", "ssn_missing", no["registry"]["ssn_missing"]),
     blank("registry.csv", "street_name_missing", no["registry"]["address_missing"]),
     size_registry_mb, md5_registry),
    ("finder_500k.csv", n(files["finder_500k.csv"]["rows"]), finder_500k_simulants, overlap_500k_simulants,
     blank("finder_500k.csv", "ssn_missing", no["finder"]["ssn_missing"]),
     blank("finder_500k.csv", "street_name_missing", no["finder"]["address_missing"]),
     size_finder500k_mb, md5_finder500k),
    ("finder_100k.csv", n(files["finder_100k.csv"]["rows"]), finder_100k_simulants, overlap_100k_simulants,
     blank("finder_100k.csv", "ssn_missing", no["finder"]["ssn_missing"]),
     blank("finder_100k.csv", "street_name_missing", no["finder"]["address_missing"]),
     size_finder100k_mb, md5_finder100k),
    (manifest["zip"]["name"], "", "", "", "", "", size_zip_mb, md5_zip),
]
header = ["File", "Rows", "People", "Shared with registry", "SSN blank (target → realised)", "Street name blank", "MB", "MD5"]
print("| " + " | ".join(header) + " |")
print("|" + "|".join(["---"] * len(header)) + "|")
for r in rows:
    print("| " + " | ".join(f"`{c}`" if i in (0, 7) and c else str(c) for i, c in enumerate(r)) + " |")
```
